record.title: A mathematical-analysis preprint reports mismatches between OpenAI’s Navier-Stokes proof and cited Lean estimates
record.summary: Bastounis, Circelli and Hansen compare OpenAI’s natural-language Navier–Stokes proof with cited Lean declarations. For Lemma 8.6, equation (8.19), they report that the manuscript states an m+4 derivative estimate while the cited Lean estimate requires m+5. For pressure-flux equation (10.19), they report a different Lean bound and proof route, including an additional localized gradient norm. They note one similar auxiliary bound in the repository does not appear to be directly used in the proposed theorem, leaving the effect on the actual proof dependency chain unresolved. The authors explicitly do not claim the natural-language blow-up proof is incorrect. This remains a source-reported critique in an arXiv preprint, without independent reproduction or established specialist consensus.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors compare OpenAI’s natural-language proof of Lemma 8.6, equation (8.19), with its cited Lean declaration at commit f9e8bc5. They report the manuscript estimate uses m+4 input derivatives while the cited Lean estimate requires m+5; this is a concrete mismatch in the stated bound, not a demonstration that the Navier–Stokes blow-up theorem is false.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that the Lean estimate cited for pressure-flux equation (10.19) has a different expression and proof route, including an additional localized gradient norm A_R. They also note that a similar auxiliary bound in the Lean repository does not appear to be used directly in the proposed Navier–Stokes theorem; traceability through the actual theorem dependency remains a key audit question.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors argue that Lean acceptance verifies the encoded formal statement, not semantic preservation of the natural-language proof. They explicitly disclaim making a claim about whether OpenAI’s natural-language proof is correct.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of the reported m+4/m+5 or pressure-flux estimate comparisons, and no reconciliation against later OpenAI repository revisions, were completed as of this review.

The preprint does not refute the underlying blow-up theorem. It reports selected formal correspondence gaps; the effect on the theorem’s actual proof dependencies remains unresolved, especially because the authors note one similar auxiliary bound is not directly used in the theorem.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported mismatches hold, a machine-checked Lean result cannot be treated as verification of the specific natural-language proof without a semantic bridge. This changes how an extraordinary mathematical claim should be evaluated, although the audit does not refute the underlying theorem.
limitations: This is an author-reported analysis in an arXiv v1 preprint; peer review and independent specialist consensus were not established.

brief.title: A mathematical-analysis preprint reports mismatches between OpenAI’s Navier-Stokes proof and cited Lean estimates
brief.why_it_matters: A formal proof establishes its encoded theorem, but it does not by itself establish that the theorem matches the natural-language argument it is meant to check. The reported estimate differences give concrete targets for independent Lean and PDE review of an extraordinary mathematical claim, while leaving the truth of the underlying blow-up result unresolved.
